experiments.name: Cryogenic He/Ne separation for groundwater noble-gas and 3H/3He dating: Ne adsorbed on a 14 K sintered-steel cold trap (+/-0.1 K), released at 100 K, in a UHV extraction line with LN2 traps
experiments.plain_name: Separate helium from neon in groundwater gas with a 14 K cold trap
experiments.description: Noble gases extracted from about 45 g of groundwater sealed in copper tubes are purified in an ultrahigh-vacuum line; water vapour and heavy gases are frozen onto liquid-nitrogen traps, and He is separated from Ne on a computer-controlled cryogenic cold trap held at 14 K (Ne adsorbed, He measured), then warmed to 100 K to release Ne, before magnetic-sector mass spectrometry (Eawag/ETH system).

requirements.rationale: The cold trap must hold 14 K for Ne adsorption and then be heated to 100 K to release Ne, so the trap temperature must span 14-100 K.
requirements.document_title: Beyerle et al. (2000) A Mass Spectrometric System for the Analysis of Noble Gases and Tritium from Water Samples, Environ. Sci. Technol. 34, 2042-2050
requirements.quote: the He and Ne phase is transferred to a cryogenic cold trap (CCT) at 14 K ... After 20 min the He fraction is transferred to the spectrometer and the CCT is heated to 100 K to release Ne

requirements.rationale: Quantitative Ne adsorption needs the trap at 14 K or colder.
requirements.document_title: Beyerle et al. (2000) A Mass Spectrometric System for the Analysis of Noble Gases and Tritium from Water Samples, Environ. Sci. Technol. 34, 2042-2050
requirements.quote: the He and Ne phase is transferred to a cryogenic cold trap (CCT) at 14 K containing a high porosity filter of sintered stainless steel (Nupro SS-2FE-5, 0.5 um) that adsorbs Ne quantitatively

requirements.rationale: The trap temperature is computer-set and must stay within 0.1 K during Ne adsorption.
requirements.document_title: Beyerle et al. (2000) A Mass Spectrometric System for the Analysis of Noble Gases and Tritium from Water Samples, Environ. Sci. Technol. 34, 2042-2050
requirements.quote: The temperature of the CCT can be set by computer control and is stable within ±0.1 K or better during Ne adsorption.

requirements.rationale: The cold trap sits in the all-metal ultrahigh-vacuum extraction and purification line.
requirements.document_title: Beyerle et al. (2000) A Mass Spectrometric System for the Analysis of Noble Gases and Tritium from Water Samples, Environ. Sci. Technol. 34, 2042-2050
requirements.quote: the copper tube is directly connected to the ultrahigh vacuum (UHV) extraction and purification line by means of a device which presses the front of the copper tube UHV-tight onto a metal cutting edge

requirements.rationale: The extraction line is pumped to about 1e-7 mbar before the sample is opened (approximate figure, so optional).
requirements.document_title: Beyerle et al. (2000) A Mass Spectrometric System for the Analysis of Noble Gases and Tritium from Water Samples, Environ. Sci. Technol. 34, 2042-2050
requirements.quote: Finally, a combination of a diaphragm (DP2) and turbomolecular pump (TP2, Pfeiffer TPU 050) reduces the pressure to about 10 -7 mbar.

requirements.rationale: Water vapour and condensable gases are frozen onto an all-metal trap and a zeolite trap cooled by liquid nitrogen (separate traps on the same line).
requirements.document_title: Beyerle et al. (2000) A Mass Spectrometric System for the Analysis of Noble Gases and Tritium from Water Samples, Environ. Sci. Technol. 34, 2042-2050
requirements.quote: The water vapor and the extracted gases are adsorbed on an all-metal trap (T1) and a trap filled with zeolite (ZEO1, Varian, molecular sieve of 5 A pore diameter), both cooled by liquid nitrogen.

sources.citation: Beyerle et al. (2000) A Mass Spectrometric System for the Analysis of Noble Gases and Tritium from Water Samples, Environ. Sci. Technol. 34, 2042-2050

reported_equipment: cryogenic cold trap (CCT) with Nupro SS-2FE-5 sintered stainless-steel filter
noncommercial 90 degree magnetic sector mass spectrometers MS1/MS2

experiments.name: Variable-temperature 57Fe Mossbauer spectroscopy (140 K to <=5 K) of 57Fe-labelled ferrihydrite transformation in anoxic paddy-soil incubations
experiments.plain_name: Track how iron rust minerals change in soil by cooling them toward 5 K for gamma-ray spectra
experiments.description: 57Fe-ferrihydrite (65 mg) is mixed into 15 g of soil and incubated anoxically; solids are frozen in liquid nitrogen, freeze-dried and measured by 57Fe Mossbauer spectroscopy at 140, 77, 45, 25, 15, 10 and <=5 K, because magnetic ordering of ferrihydrite and secondary Fe(II)/Fe(III) phases only appears at the lowest temperatures.

requirements.rationale: The temperature profile runs from 140 K down to 5 K; the cryostat must cover this whole window.
requirements.document_title: Notini et al. (2023) A New Approach for Investigating Iron Mineral Transformations in Soils and Sediments Using 57Fe-Labeled Minerals and 57Fe Mossbauer Spectroscopy, Environ. Sci. Technol. 57, 10008-10018
requirements.location: Results, fitting of temperature-profile spectra; Figure 3 caption
requirements.quote: Spectra collected at 140, 77, 45, 25, and 15 K were fitted using the extended Voigt-based fitting (xVBF) model. ... Spectra were collected at 25, 10, and ≤5 K.

requirements.rationale: The Fe(II) octet only forms below 15 K and the decisive spectra were taken at <=5 K.
requirements.document_title: Notini et al. (2023) A New Approach for Investigating Iron Mineral Transformations in Soils and Sediments Using 57Fe-Labeled Minerals and 57Fe Mossbauer Spectroscopy, Environ. Sci. Technol. 57, 10008-10018
requirements.quote: The 5 K Mössbauer spectra of samples incubated for 12 weeks revealed the formation of octets

requirements.rationale: Routine incubation-series spectra were collected at 77 K.
requirements.document_title: Notini et al. (2023) A New Approach for Investigating Iron Mineral Transformations in Soils and Sediments Using 57Fe-Labeled Minerals and 57Fe Mossbauer Spectroscopy, Environ. Sci. Technol. 57, 10008-10018
requirements.quote: Spectra were collected at 77 K.

sources.citation: Notini et al. (2023) A New Approach for Investigating Iron Mineral Transformations in Soils and Sediments Using 57Fe-Labeled Minerals and 57Fe Mossbauer Spectroscopy, Environ. Sci. Technol. 57, 10008-10018, doi:10.1021/acs.est.3c00434

reported_equipment: MBraun anoxic glovebox (N2 atmosphere, <5 ppm O2)
57Fe Mossbauer spectrometer and cryostat (models given only in the Supporting Information, not in the main text)

experiments.name: GO-SHIP seawater nutrient (N, P, Si) sample preservation by rapid freezing in a deep freezer at -20 C or colder
experiments.plain_name: Freeze seawater samples so their nutrients can be measured back on land
experiments.description: When nutrient samples from hydrographic cruises cannot be analysed within two to three days, the 3/4-filled, capped bottles are frozen as soon and as rapidly as possible in a deep freezer at -20 C or colder with good air circulation, kept in gridded racks, and thawed in air before continuous-flow analysis.

requirements.rationale: The storage space must reach -20 C (253.15 K) or colder.
requirements.document_title: Hydes et al. (2010) Determination of dissolved nutrients (N, P, Si) in seawater with high precision and inter-comparability using gas-segmented continuous flow analysers, GO-SHIP Repeat Hydrography Manual (IOCCP Report 14)
requirements.quote: Before freezing ensure that sample bottles are no more than 3/4 full and firmly capped. A deep freezer (at least -20 oC) should be used.

requirements.rationale: Lowest achievable storage temperature must be -20 C or colder.
requirements.document_title: Hydes et al. (2010) Determination of dissolved nutrients (N, P, Si) in seawater with high precision and inter-comparability using gas-segmented continuous flow analysers, GO-SHIP Repeat Hydrography Manual (IOCCP Report 14)
requirements.quote: A deep freezer (at least -20 oC) should be used. Good air circulation around the bottles in the freezer is important.

requirements.rationale: Freezing relies on air circulation around the bottles in an atmospheric freezer, not an evacuated chamber.

experiments.name: Isobaric-isothermal synthesis of sI methane hydrate from sieved ice powder and CH4 at 3.5-15 MPa and 268-271 K for 3 weeks, quenched in liquid nitrogen
experiments.plain_name: Grow methane ice-cage crystals from frozen water and gas under high pressure
experiments.description: Ice spheres made by spraying water into liquid nitrogen are loaded into a 6.7 mm Al vial inside a precooled pressure vessel whose temperature is held by a circulating cryostat bath, pressurized with CH4 (3.5-15 MPa) at 268 K (H2O) or 271 K (D2O) for 3 weeks, then quenched in liquid nitrogen, depressurized, ground under LN2 and stored under LN2 for diffraction and Raman analysis.

requirements.rationale: H2O-based hydrates were formed at 268 K (Table 1 formation temperature).
requirements.document_title: Qin, Hartmann and Kuhs, Cage occupancies of methane hydrates: results from synchrotron X-ray diffraction and Raman spectroscopy, Proc. 8th Int. Conf. on Gas Hydrates (ICGH8-2014), Beijing (arXiv:1803.02244)

requirements.rationale: The highest formation pressure was 15 MPa, which the sample vessel must withstand.
requirements.document_title: Qin, Hartmann and Kuhs, Cage occupancies of methane hydrates: results from synchrotron X-ray diffraction and Raman spectroscopy, Proc. 8th Int. Conf. on Gas Hydrates (ICGH8-2014), Beijing (arXiv:1803.02244)

requirements.rationale: Each formation reaction ran for 3 weeks (504 h) at constant pressure and temperature.
requirements.document_title: Qin, Hartmann and Kuhs, Cage occupancies of methane hydrates: results from synchrotron X-ray diffraction and Raman spectroscopy, Proc. 8th Int. Conf. on Gas Hydrates (ICGH8-2014), Beijing (arXiv:1803.02244)
requirements.quote: During the reaction, pressure was manually maintained to the set point within 0.1-0.2 MPa. All formation reactions ran for 3 weeks.

requirements.rationale: Ice powder is loaded in an Al vial with 6.7 mm inner diameter inside the pressure vessel.
requirements.document_title: Qin, Hartmann and Kuhs, Cage occupancies of methane hydrates: results from synchrotron X-ray diffraction and Raman spectroscopy, Proc. 8th Int. Conf. on Gas Hydrates (ICGH8-2014), Beijing (arXiv:1803.02244)
requirements.quote: Ice particles were filled into an Al-vial with an inner diameter of 6.7 mm or in a larger PFA-jar, which was inserted into a precooled custom-built pressure vessel where temperature was controlled by a circulating cryostat bath.

requirements.rationale: Ice spheres are made in LN2 and the cell is quenched in LN2 at the end (separate dewar step).
requirements.document_title: Qin, Hartmann and Kuhs, Cage occupancies of methane hydrates: results from synchrotron X-ray diffraction and Raman spectroscopy, Proc. 8th Int. Conf. on Gas Hydrates (ICGH8-2014), Beijing (arXiv:1803.02244)
requirements.quote: At the completion of the reaction, the pressure cell was rapidly quenched in liq. N 2 and pressure was concomitantly released.

sources.citation: Qin, Hartmann and Kuhs, Cage occupancies of methane hydrates: results from synchrotron X-ray diffraction and Raman spectroscopy, Proc. 8th Int. Conf. on Gas Hydrates (ICGH8-2014), Beijing (arXiv:1803.02244)

experiments.name: Confocal Raman determination of methane large/small cage occupancy in recovered hydrate on a Linkam THMS600 stage at 113 +/- 0.1 K
experiments.plain_name: Count methane molecules trapped in ice cages with laser light at 113 K
experiments.description: Recovered methane hydrate, stored under liquid nitrogen, is placed on a Linkam THMS600 cooling stage and measured at 113 +/- 0.1 K with a LabRAM HR800 (488 nm, 50x long-working-distance objective); the C-H stretching band splits at about 2901 and 2913 cm-1 into large- and small-cage contributions.

requirements.rationale: Spectra are taken with the hydrate held at 113 K so it does not decompose.
requirements.document_title: Qin, Hartmann and Kuhs, Cage occupancies of methane hydrates: results from synchrotron X-ray diffraction and Raman spectroscopy, Proc. 8th Int. Conf. on Gas Hydrates (ICGH8-2014), Beijing (arXiv:1803.02244)

requirements.rationale: Measurement temperature held to +/-0.1 K.
requirements.document_title: Qin, Hartmann and Kuhs, Cage occupancies of methane hydrates: results from synchrotron X-ray diffraction and Raman spectroscopy, Proc. 8th Int. Conf. on Gas Hydrates (ICGH8-2014), Beijing (arXiv:1803.02244)

experiments.name: FC/ZFC/LTC remanence, AC susceptibility and low-temperature hysteresis (5-300 K, 5 T SIRM) of gas-hydrate-bearing sediments from IODP Site U1519C on an MPMS XL-7
experiments.plain_name: Read the magnetic minerals in deeply buried gas-hydrate mud between 5 K and room temperature
experiments.description: Thirteen sediment samples from 587-618 mbsf are given a 5 T SIRM (field-cooled, zero-field-cooled and room-temperature low-temperature-cycling protocols) and measured between 5 and 300 K; a subset gets AC susceptibility (1, 10, 111 Hz) and hysteresis loops at 5, 70, 130 and 300 K to +/-1 T, to identify magnetite and iron sulfides.

requirements.rationale: All protocols cool to 5 K and warm back to 300 K.
requirements.document_title: Liu, Li and Xu (2025) Low-temperature magnetic properties of deeply buried gas hydrate bearing sediments: a case study from IODP expedition 375 site U1519C in the Hikurangi subduction zone, New Zealand, Frontiers in Earth Science
requirements.quote: For the FC measurements, samples were cooled from 300 K to 5 K in a 5 T field to impart a saturation isothermal remanent magnetization (SIRM), after which the remanence was recorded during zero-field warming to 300 K.

requirements.rationale: The lowest measurement temperature is 5 K.
requirements.document_title: Liu, Li and Xu (2025) Low-temperature magnetic properties of deeply buried gas hydrate bearing sediments: a case study from IODP expedition 375 site U1519C in the Hikurangi subduction zone, New Zealand, Frontiers in Earth Science
requirements.quote: For the ZFC protocol, samples were first cooled to 5 K in zero field, then subjected to a 5 T pulse to impart a SIRM, with remanence subsequently measured during warming in zero field.

requirements.rationale: SIRM is imparted in a 5 T field.
requirements.document_title: Liu, Li and Xu (2025) Low-temperature magnetic properties of deeply buried gas hydrate bearing sediments: a case study from IODP expedition 375 site U1519C in the Hikurangi subduction zone, New Zealand, Frontiers in Earth Science
requirements.quote: The LTC procedure involved magnetizing samples at 300 K in a 5 T field, cooling them to 5 K in zero field, and then measuring remanence during stepwise warming to 300 K in 2 K increments.

requirements.rationale: AC susceptibility at 1-111 Hz was measured on a subset of nine samples.
requirements.document_title: Liu, Li and Xu (2025) Low-temperature magnetic properties of deeply buried gas hydrate bearing sediments: a case study from IODP expedition 375 site U1519C in the Hikurangi subduction zone, New Zealand, Frontiers in Earth Science
requirements.quote: AC susceptibility was measured on this subset at frequencies of 1, 10, and 111 Hz during warming after zero-field cooling to 5 K.

sources.citation: Liu, Li and Xu (2025) Low-temperature magnetic properties of deeply buried gas hydrate bearing sediments: a case study from IODP expedition 375 site U1519C in the Hikurangi subduction zone, New Zealand, Frontiers in Earth Science

experiments.name: Room-temperature SIRM cycling and 5 K LT-SIRM (ZFC/FC, 2.5 T) of iron-sulfide-bearing gas-hydrate sediments, IODP Site C0008, Nankai Trough
experiments.plain_name: Detect magnetic iron-sulfide grains in seafloor mud by cooling them to 5 K in a 2.5 T field
experiments.description: Twenty-one selected sediment samples are given a 2.5 T SIRM at 300 K and cycled to 5 K in near-zero field, then a 2.5 T LT-SIRM is imparted at 5 K (ZFC) and after cooling in 2.5 T (FC) and measured on warming to 300 K in a Quantum Design MPMS; NRM/ARM of 7 cc cubes are measured on a 2G SQUID cryogenic magnetometer in a shielded room.

requirements.rationale: Remanence is cycled between room temperature (300 K) and 5 K.
requirements.document_title: Kars and Kodama (2015) Rock magnetic characterization of ferrimagnetic iron sulfides in gas hydrate-bearing marine sediments at Site C0008, Nankai Trough, Pacific Ocean, off-coast Japan, Earth, Planets and Space
requirements.quote: The sample is then cooled down to 5 K in a 2.5 T magnetic field, and the LT-SIRM is measured during warming to 300 K (FC for field cooled).

requirements.rationale: LT-SIRM is imparted at 5 K.
requirements.document_title: Kars and Kodama (2015) Rock magnetic characterization of ferrimagnetic iron sulfides in gas hydrate-bearing marine sediments at Site C0008, Nankai Trough, Pacific Ocean, off-coast Japan, Earth, Planets and Space
requirements.quote: A low temperature (LT)-SIRM was imparted at 5 K at 2.5 T.

requirements.rationale: All SIRMs are imparted at 2.5 T.
requirements.document_title: Kars and Kodama (2015) Rock magnetic characterization of ferrimagnetic iron sulfides in gas hydrate-bearing marine sediments at Site C0008, Nankai Trough, Pacific Ocean, off-coast Japan, Earth, Planets and Space
requirements.quote: A cooling-warming cycle of a saturation isothermal remanent magnetization (SIRM) imparted at room temperature (300 K) at 2.5 T was first measured in a zero magnetic field (trapped field <150 uT).

requirements.rationale: NRM and ARM are measured in a SQUID cryogenic magnetometer inside a shielded room (separate instrument from the MPMS).
requirements.document_title: Kars and Kodama (2015) Rock magnetic characterization of ferrimagnetic iron sulfides in gas hydrate-bearing marine sediments at Site C0008, Nankai Trough, Pacific Ocean, off-coast Japan, Earth, Planets and Space
requirements.quote: Natural remanent magnetization (NRM) and anhysteretic remanent magnetization (ARM) were measured with a 2G SQUID cryogenic magnetometer in the shielded room (noise level ~10-10 Am2).

experiments.plain_name: Grow a metre-sized block of sea ice in a walk-in freezer to follow its carbon

experiments.description: Columns (6.55 cm diameter, 44 cm tall) of artificial seawater (31.28 g/L) on an orbital shaker in a 1 C room are frozen from the top for 19 h by an aluminium cooling element fed by a cryothermostat bath at -5.1 +/- 0.1 C; the ice is lifted out, centrifuged and some cores are kept at -20 C for micro-CT.

experiments.name: Low-temperature demagnetization (10 min liquid-nitrogen soak, zero field) of one-inch lava cores in Tsunakawa-Shaw paleointensity experiments
experiments.plain_name: Dunk lava rock cores in liquid nitrogen to strip weak magnetism before measuring ancient field strength
experiments.description: Before each stepwise AF demagnetization of NRM, ARM and laboratory TRM, one-inch Hawaiian lava specimens are soaked in liquid nitrogen for 10 min and warmed at room temperature for 30 min in zero field (low-temperature demagnetization, LTD), removing multidomain magnetite remanence; remanence is measured with DSPIN/ASPIN spinner magnetometers with AF to 180 mT.

requirements.rationale: LTD is done by soaking the specimen in liquid nitrogen.

requirements.rationale: Specimens are cut from standard one-inch paleomagnetic cores.

notes: Quotes were read from the full texts (Eawag PDF text extraction, PMC page, GO-SHIP PDF text extraction, arXiv full text, and Undermind full-text readers for the Frontiers/EPS/Nature Communications papers); PDF text-extraction artifacts were normalised (e.g. '±' rendered as '(' in the Beyerle PDF). Web search, Tavily and Lune quotas were exhausted during this run, so the 2G 755 u-channel SRM, Stanley 2009 WHOI noble-gas, Hirai 2001 methane-hydrate DAC (repository under maintenance) and the CGS hydrate PXRD (403) ideas could not be sourced verbatim and were replaced. Liquid-nitrogen steps that happen in a separate dewar (quench, LN2 traps, storage) are marked mandatory=false so they do not exclude the main cryogenic machine. Kon18 tank footprint 105 x 95 cm is converted to a circumscribed diameter of 141.6 cm per the shared sample.diameter.max rule.
